hero.subtitle: San Clemente workers who get hurt on the job — whether at a jobsite near I-5, a shop off Avenida Pico, or a delivery route through town — often have more than one path to recovery. We can connect you with an independent attorney who looks at the whole picture, not just workers' comp.

about.title: San Clemente Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: San Clemente's mix of construction, retail, hospitality, and coastal commercial activity means workplace injuries here can look very different from case to case — a fall on a wet floor near El Camino Real, a delivery driver injured near the I-5 interchange, or an equipment accident on a job site. In most cases, California's workers' compensation system is the exclusive way to seek benefits from your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But when a third party contributed to the accident — a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver — a separate injury claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly; we're a free service that connects injured workers in San Clemente with an independent attorney who can explain which options might apply to your specific situation, at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney About Your Case

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can support a separate claim outside that system.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and separate third-party injury claims carry a 2-year deadline, so timing can affect what options remain open.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: Employers cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury or pursuing benefits, and an attorney can help you understand your protections if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt at work near the I-5 corridor while making deliveries — does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. If your injury happened while driving for work and another driver was involved, that could open the door to a third-party claim in addition to your workers' comp benefits. An independent attorney can review the details of what happened on the road to see if that applies.

items.question: Can I still get workers' comp if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: Generally yes — California's workers' compensation system usually doesn't require proving fault to receive benefits from your employer. That's different from a third-party claim, where negligence has to be shown.

items.question: What if my employer discourages me from reporting my injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you're facing pressure not to report, it's worth speaking with an independent attorney who can explain your rights and the reporting timeline.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, the connection service is free. Attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
